content: Agathosma betulina, previously known as Barosma betulina, is a flowering plant belonging to the Rutaceae family. It is native to the lower elevation mountainous regions of western South Africa, where it thrives near streams in fynbos habitats. This plant is an evergreen shrub that can grow up to 2 meters in height. Its leaves are arranged oppositely, are rounded in shape, and measure approximately 20 millimeters in both length and width. The flowers of Agathosma betulina are either white or pale pink in color and consist of five petals. The fruit is a five-parted capsule that splits open to release seeds. Commonly referred to as round leaf buchu, this plant has historically been utilized both as a flavoring agent and as an herbal remedy. A closely related species, Agathosma crenulata (formerly Barosma crenulata), known as oval leaf buchu, has been used for similar purposes. Although wild populations of Agathosma betulina remain abundant, they are being harvested at a rate that exceeds their natural reproductive capacity. This overharvesting has raised concerns about potential scarcity, prompting efforts to cultivate the plant. The essential oils and extracts derived from its leaves are widely used as flavoring agents in teas, candies, and a South African liquor known as buchu brandy. The two primary essential oils found in Agathosma betulina are isomenthone and diosphenol. The plant extract is reported to have a flavor reminiscent of blackcurrant. Historically, it has been employed in traditional medicine for the treatment of urinary tract disorders and for wound care.
